patterns: Two Pointers (opposite-direction for sorted arrays/palindromes; same-direction/fast-slow for in-place ops & linked lists) + Sliding Window (expand right, shrink left, track window state) + Arrays & Hashing (hashmap/hashset for O(1) lookups — frequency counting, complement lookups, anagram grouping)
notes: Pure cold-attempt discipline starts here. No review load yet — you have nothing banked. Arrays & Hashing problems are mostly quick (many under 15 min) so they absorb into the week without blowing up hours much.

patterns: Binary Search (unified left<=right template; same skeleton for exact match, left-bound, right-bound, and 'search on the answer') + Linked List Techniques (dummy head, fast/slow, iterative reversal)
notes: Start logging every problem in the Tracker. Begin reviewing your 2-3 shakiest Week 1 problems.

patterns: Monotonic Stack (next greater/smaller element) + Monotonic Queue (O(n) sliding-window max/min) + Prefix Sum / Difference Array (range queries/updates) + Binary Tree recursion mindset (traversal vs. decompose)
notes: This is the most 'aha' week for tree recursion — force yourself to write the decompose-style definition before coding.

patterns: BFS (level-order w/ queue + visited set, shortest path in unweighted graphs/grids) + Backtracking (path / choices / end-condition skeleton — subsets, combinations, permutations, N-Queens)
notes: Backtracking is volume-heavy on purpose — the skeleton is identical across subtypes, so reps compound fast once it clicks.

patterns: Dynamic Programming Part 1 — the 3-step framework (base case -> precise dp definition -> state transition), top-down memoized recursion vs. bottom-up dp array, classic 1D DP (climbing stairs, house robber, coin change) + intro 2D DP
notes: Slow down here. DP is the pattern most candidates fake their way through — insist on writing the dp definition in a comment before any code.

patterns: DP Part 2 (subsequence DP, knapsack variants) + Graph algorithms (Union-Find w/ path compression, topological sort / Kahn's, Dijkstra, plus deeper graph traversal: Clone Graph, Surrounded Regions, Reconstruct Itinerary, Cheapest Flights Within K Stops) + Greedy (interval scheduling) — closes out the core pattern set
notes: Still zero company-tag time this week on purpose. Breadth across all patterns comes first; tagging is a later supplement, not a driver. Graph got a deeper pass here since it was thin before.

patterns: New patterns that round out all-round coverage: Heap/Priority Queue, Trie, Intervals, Bit Manipulation, Design problems (LRU Cache, etc.), plus advanced Binary Tree (serialize/deserialize, construct from traversals, max path sum, kth smallest in BST) — these show up constantly but weren't fully covered in weeks 1-6
notes: This week exists because 'all-round' isn't complete without heaps/tries/intervals/bit-manip/advanced trees. Company-repo browsing (see that tab) is light exposure only, not the focus.

patterns: No new pattern — full-system spaced review across all 14+ patterns, timed mixed mock sets (2 random-pattern problems / 45 min, no notes) pulled from a general mixed pool, plus a light final pass through your target companies' repo lists to catch obvious blind spots.
notes: This week is about retention and unknown-pattern reflexes, not coverage. Every Tracker row marked 'DUE' takes priority over anything new.
